reason: Before the fix, REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY and YYYY, so lone 'Y' falls through to the timezone-offset fallback, producing a UTC offset string instead of the literal character 'Y'.
After the fix, REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY explicitly, so a lone 'Y' is not captured by the regex and is preserved as a literal character in the output.

The PR is a pure refactoring that extracts tryDecodeURIComponent into a utility; the decoding logic (check for '%', then decode) is unchanged, so percent-encoded route parameters are still decoded correctly.
Same refactoring as js_0011; the tryDecodeURIComponent utility in utils/url.ts contains the identical logic, so decoded parameters work correctly after the PR.
Before the fix, SortedEntry#reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates the in-memory @score, so entry.score and entry.at return stale pre-reschedule values.
After the fix, @score = at.to_f is set after zincrby, so the in-memory entry immediately reflects the new reschedule time.
The PR changes only parseRangesSpecifier (Range header parsing) to trim whitespace around commas; Content-Type header parsing with charset parameters is completely unaffected.
Same as jvm_0007; the Range header PR does not touch Content-Type parsing, which continues to correctly parse charset parameters.
The PR only changes error/warning log messages in ComposerRepository to include sanitized filenames; archive timestamp handling is completely unrelated and already preserves source timestamps.
Same logging-only PR as kbc_0007; re-archiving timestamps are unaffected by changes to error message formatting.
The PR changes CredentialCacheKey.IsPrefix path comparison to case-sensitive; JSON deserialization (JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync) is in a completely different subsystem and unaffected.
Same CredentialCache PR as kbc_0009; sync and async JSON deserialization are unaffected by credential cache path comparison changes.
The PR fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursors; INET subnet containment operators (<<= ANY) are in a completely different part of CockroachDB and unaffected.
Same cursor PR as kbd_0013; INET network containment (>>= ANY) is unaffected by the cursor fix.
Before the fix, NO_PROXY entries like '::1' are prefixed with a wildcard producing 'all://*::1', which URL parsing cannot interpret as a valid pattern, causing an error during client construction.
After the fix, IPv6 NO_PROXY entries like '::1' are detected and formatted as 'all://[::1]', which is a valid URL pattern, so client construction succeeds.

Before the fix, Series.str.match rejects regex flags other than IGNORECASE (like re.DOTALL) because the flag equality check against the compiled pattern fails, raising a ValueError instead of performing the match.
After the fix, flags like re.DOTALL are properly handled; the accessor no longer rejects non-IGNORECASE flags, and 'a.c' with DOTALL correctly matches 'a\nc'.

Before the fix, prepare_steps does not update prev_task/prev_res after processing a group in the middle of a chain, which corrupts the result parent linkage and breaks the serialized result tree structure for subsequent groups.
After the fix, prev_task and prev_res are correctly updated after each group in prepare_steps, preserving the result tree structure through serialization and deserialization.

The test uses '--' after value1 and value2 (not as the first argument), so the standard double-dash handling already works correctly; the value_terminator properly stops the first positional and the second positional collects '--check'.
Same test as rg_0005; the PR fixes the edge case where '--' is the first argument, but this test has values before '--', so it continues to pass after the fix.

Before the fix, nvim_set_option_value('background', bg, {}) triggers OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands when the OSC 11 response arrives after startup, matching the test's expected behavior of both events firing.
After the fix, 'noautocmd set background=' suppresses OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands when OSC 11 arrives, so the test expecting both autocommands to fire will fail because neither fires.
The PR only reorders compile-time checks in Ecto.Schema to avoid reading @derive unnecessarily; runtime changeset validation (cast + validate_required) is completely unaffected.
Same compile-time dependency ordering PR as sa_0007; required field validation at runtime is unaffected by changes to compile-time attribute reading order.
